Owner-only FREE plan grant/upgrade. Sets a user's plan directly in our

schema.title: Response Admin Grant Plan V2 Admin Grant Plan Post

post.description:
SEC-01 / AUTH-02 — revoke EVERY active sk_live_ key belonging to an email.

Why this exists: there was no operator primitive for it. The only bulk revoke was
DELETE /v2/self-serve/account, which also closes the account and NULLs customer_email
(destroying the join key), and which could only be reached by first minting an ssv_
token through the very hole SEC-01 closes. AUTH-02's account merge needs to retire the
losing side's keys without closing anything, so it needs this.

Guarded by the same static ADMIN_GRANT_TOKEN as /v2/admin/grant-plan.

Idempotent by construction: the UPDATE carries `AND key_status <> 'revoked'`, so a
repeat call neither re-stamps revoked_at nor double-counts. Keys already revoked come
back under `already_revoked` so the caller can still see the full picture.

Unknown email -> 200 with empty lists, NOT 404. The merge caller routinely asks about a
losing email that never had an engine account at all; making the benign case an error
would force every caller to special-case it. `account_ids: []` states plainly that
nothing matched.

delete.description:
Close the account: revoke every key immediately, invalidate portal access, redact the profile.

SOFT delete (account_status='closed'), not a row DROP. Billing and usage records are RETAINED —
they are required for tax/accounting/audit — and the response says so explicitly rather than
implying a wipe that did not happen.

HONEST LIMIT: this does NOT cancel a subscription at the payment provider (Stripe/Polar own that
state; cancelling only our mirror row would desync and the customer would keep being charged
while believing they were not). When a subscription is still live we return
billing.action_required=true plus the portal path, and say so in plain language.
